\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[First-coordinate slice]
\lean{FABL.f₂FirstCoordinateSlice}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂BooleanFunction, FABL.𝔽₂}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p071-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p086-b004
}
For a function $f:\\mathbb F_2^{n+1}\\to\\mathbb F_2$ and $b\\in\\mathbb F_2$, define
its slice at first coordinate $b$ to be the function on $\\mathbb F_2^n$ sending $x$ to
$f(b,x)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Indicator after shifting coordinates]
\lean{FABL.f₂CubeOfFinset_tailFrequency}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.f₂CubeOfFinset, FABL.tailFrequency}
\difficulty{4}
For every natural number $n$ and every finite set $T\subseteq\mathrm{Fin}(n)$, the
indicator vector of the set obtained by shifting each element of $T$ one place into
$\mathrm{Fin}(n+1)$ is the vector whose initial coordinate is $0$ and whose remaining
coordinates are the indicator vector of $T$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Indicator after adjoining the initial coordinate]
\lean{FABL.f₂CubeOfFinset_insert_zero_tailFrequency}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.f₂CubeOfFinset, FABL.tailFrequency}
\difficulty{4}
For every natural number $n$ and every finite set $T\subseteq\mathrm{Fin}(n)$, the
binary indicator vector of the set consisting of the initial coordinate together with
the one-place shifts of the elements of $T$ is the vector of length $n+1$ whose initial
coordinate is $1$ and whose remaining coordinates are the indicator vector of $T$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Coefficient of the zero-coordinate slice]
\lean{FABL.anfCoeff_firstCoordinateSlice_zero}
\label{FABL.anfCoeff_firstCoordinateSlice_zero}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂BooleanFunction, FABL.anfCoeff, FABL.f₂CubeOfFinset_tailFrequency, FABL.f₂FirstCoordinateSlice, FABL.tailFrequency}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\{0,1\}^{n+1}\to\mathbb F_2$, and let
$S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$. Write $S^+$ for the corresponding set of tail coordinates
in the $(n+1)$-dimensional cube. The algebraic normal form coefficient indexed by $S$ of
the slice of $f$ whose first coordinate is $0$ equals the coefficient of $f$ indexed by
$S^+$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Coefficient of the one-coordinate slice]
\lean{FABL.anfCoeff_firstCoordinateSlice_one}
\label{FABL.anfCoeff_firstCoordinateSlice_one}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂BooleanFunction, FABL.anfCoeff, FABL.anfCoeff_firstCoordinateSlice_zero, FABL.f₂CubeOfFinset, FABL.f₂CubeOfFinset_insert_zero_tailFrequency, FABL.f₂FirstCoordinateSlice, FABL.tailFrequency, FABL.zero_notMem_tailFrequency}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\{0,1\}^{n+1}\to\mathbb F_2$, and let
$S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$. Write $S^+$ for the corresponding set of tail coordinates
in the $(n+1)$-dimensional cube. The algebraic normal form coefficient indexed by $S$ of
the slice of $f$ whose first coordinate is $1$ equals the sum over $4\mathbb F_2$ of
the coefficients of $f$ indexed by $S^+$ and by $S^+\cup\{0\}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Hamming norm of coordinate slices]
\lean{FABL.hammingNorm_firstCoordinateSlices}
\label{FABL.hammingNorm_firstCoordinateSlices}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂BooleanFunction, FABL.f₂FirstCoordinateSlice, FABL.f₂OneSupport, FABL.hammingNorm_eq_card_f₂OneSupport, FABL.𝔽₂}
\difficulty{4}
For every $n\ge 0$ and every function $f:\mathbb F_2^{n+1}\to\mathbb F_2$, let $f_0$ and
$f_1$ be its restrictions to inputs whose first coordinate is respectively $0$ and $1$,
viewed as functions on $\mathbb F_2^n$. Then the Hamming norm of $f$ is the sum of the
Hamming norms of $f_0$ and $f_1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Degree bound for the zero slice]
\lean{FABL.firstCoordinateSlice_zero_degree_le}
\label{FABL.firstCoordinateSlice_zero_degree_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂BooleanFunction, FABL.algebraicDegree, FABL.algebraicDegree_le_iff, FABL.anfCoeff, FABL.anfCoeff_firstCoordinateSlice_zero, FABL.functionAlgebraicDegree, FABL.f₂FirstCoordinateSlice, FABL.tailFrequency}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n,k\in\mathbb N$ and let $f:\mathbb F_2^{n+1}\to\mathbb F_2$. If the algebraic
degree of $f$ in its algebraic normal form is at most $k$, then the algebraic degree of
the function $x\mapsto f(0,x)$ is at most $k$.
\end{theorem}

Let $n,k\in\mathbb{N}$ and let $f:\mathbb{F}_2^{n+1}\to\mathbb{F}_2$ have algebraic
degree at most $k$. If the slice obtained by fixing the first coordinate to $1$ is
identically zero, then the slice obtained by fixing it to $0$ has algebraic degree at
most $k-1$, where subtraction is truncated in $\mathbb{N}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Nonzero function has a nonzero coefficient]
\lean{FABL.exists_anfCoeff_ne_zero_of_ne_zero}

Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $f:\mathbb F_2^n\to\mathbb F_2$ be a nonzero
function. Then at least one coefficient in the algebraic normal form of $f$ is nonzero.
\end{theorem}

Let $n,k\in\mathbb{N}$ and let $f:\mathbb{F}_2^{n+1}\to\mathbb{F}_2$. Suppose the slice
of $f$ with first coordinate $0$ is identically zero, while its slice with first
coordinate $1$ is not identically zero. If the algebraic degree of $f$ is at most $k$,
then $0<k$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Vanishing coordinate slices imply vanishing]
\lean{FABL.function_eq_zero_of_both_firstCoordinateSlices_zero}
\label{FABL.function_eq_zero_of_both_firstCoordinateSlices_zero}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂BooleanFunction, FABL.f₂FirstCoordinateSlice}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $f$ be a function from the $(n+1)$-dimensional
Boolean cube over $\mathbb{F}_2$ to $\mathbb{F}_2$. If both functions on the
$n$-dimensional cube obtained by fixing the first coordinate of $f$ to $0$ and to $1$
are identically zero, then $f$ is identically zero.
\end{theorem}

Let $f:\mathbb F_2^n\to\mathbb F_2$ be a nonzero Boolean function, and suppose its
algebraic degree (the maximum size of a set indexing a nonzero coefficient in its
algebraic normal form) is at most $k$. Then $2^{n-k}\le \|f\|_0$, where $\|f\|_0$ is the
Hamming norm, the number of inputs on which $f$ is nonzero.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Nonzero probability and Hamming norm]
\lean{FABL.uniformProbability_ne_zero_eq_hammingNorm_ratio}
\label{FABL.uniformProbability_ne_zero_eq_hammingNorm_ratio}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂BooleanFunction, FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.relativeHammingDist, FABL.uniformProbability, FABL.uniformProbability_ne_eq_relativeHammingDist}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and let $f:\mathbb{F}_2^n\to\mathbb{F}_2$. The uniform probability
that $f$ is nonzero equals its Hamming norm divided by the size of the domain:
$\Pr(f\ne0)=\frac{\|f\|_0}{2^n}$, where $\|f\|_0$ is the number of inputs on which $f$
is nonzero.
\end{theorem}

nonzero with algebraic degree at most $k$. Under the uniform distribution on $\\mathbb
F_2^n$, the probability that $f$ is nonzero is at least $2^{-k}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Sum of all algebraic normal form coefficients]
\lean{FABL.anfCoeff_univ_eq_sum_f₂BooleanFunction}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂BooleanFunction, FABL.anfCoeff, FABL.f₂CubeEquivFinset, FABL.f₂CubeOfFinset, FABL.f₂Support}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb F_2$. The sum of all
algebraic normal form coefficients of $f$ equals the sum of the values of $f$ over all
inputs in the cube.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Function sum and support cardinality]
\lean{FABL.sum_f₂BooleanFunction_eq_card_f₂OneSupport}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂BooleanFunction, FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.f₂OneSupport, FABL.𝔽₂}
\difficulty{4}
Let $f$ be a function from the binary cube of dimension $n$ to $\\mathbb F_2$. The sum
of $f$ over all inputs equals, in $\\mathbb F_2$, the cardinality of the set of inputs
on which $f$ equals $1$.
\end{theorem}

    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p149-b004}
Let $n$ be a positive integer and let $f:\mathbb{F}_2^n\to\mathbb{F}_2$. The algebraic
degree of $f$ equals $n$ if and only if the coefficient of the monomial involving all
$n$ coordinates in its algebraic normal form is nonzero.
\end{theorem}
